findings.title: The fallback sync schema strips all token fields except access_token
findings.body: `z.string().toString()` is a computed object key, not a Zod catch-all declaration; it evaluates to the same string (effectively "[object Object]") for both entries. Consequently, in credential-sync mode Zod's default object behavior strips response fields such as `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, and provider-specific fields. The helper then inserts a fake `refresh_token`. Callers persist this reduced object, losing expiry/refresh-token information and causing repeated refreshes or invalid credentials (for example, Zoom subsequently calculates expiry from an absent `expires_in`). Use a schema with `.passthrough()`/`.catchall()` and preserve the existing refresh token when the sync response intentionally omits it.

findings.title: Google credential sync treats a Fetch Response as a parsed token payload
findings.body: When syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the native `fetch()` Response. This code still reads `res.data`, which only exists on the normal Google client response, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws. Any expired Google Calendar credential in sync mode therefore fails before it can make a calendar request. Parse and validate the sync endpoint's JSON response before accessing its token fields, while retaining the normal provider-response path.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends a credential ID as the Cal.com user ID to the sync endpoint
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects its third argument to be the credential owner’s user ID and sends it as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId` (the Credential primary key). The external app store will look up the wrong user and cannot return that user's refreshed Bigin credentials; IDs can also coincidentally refer to a different user. Pass `credential.userId` through this method instead.

findings.title: HubSpot sync casts an unparsed Fetch Response into a HubSpot token
findings.body: With credential sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `Response`, but this code casts it directly to `HubspotToken` and then reads `expiresIn` and `accessToken`. Those fields are undefined on `Response`, so it persists an invalid credential and configures HubSpot with an undefined access token. The sync response must be decoded to JSON and mapped to HubSpot's token representation before calculating expiry and updating the credential.

findings.title: Salesforce CalendarService references prisma without importing it
findings.body: The newly added token-refresh persistence call uses `prisma.credential.update`, but this module has no `@calcom/prisma` import. This is an unresolved identifier and prevents the app-store package from type-checking/building, blocking deployment of the PR.
